reports.text: Portable AP chest. Bilateral perihilar airspace opacities in a butterfly distribution with interstitial septal lines at both bases. Cardiac silhouette enlarged. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 12/20/2024.

72 y/o man with CAD (inferior STEMI 2022 with RCA stent, earlier LAD stent), stage 4 CKD, tertiary hyperparathyroidism treated with surgery, anemia of CKD on darbepoetin, and long-standing type 2 diabetes with a past right foot osteomyelitis. His daughter brought him in for a week of worsening breathlessness. He can no longer lie flat and has been sleeping sitting up in his recliner, and he wakes at night short of breath. He gets winded walking short distances now. No fever, cough or chest pain. No recent medication changes. Uses no alcohol or tobacco. Per his daughter he has been more tired, his feet and ankles swell more as the day goes on, and he is up at night to urinate. Eating less, but no weight loss, nausea or vomiting.

Exam: HR 104 and regular, BP 138/82. Short of breath, using accessory muscles. End-expiratory crackles at both lung bases; no wheeze or rhonchi. Apical impulse displaced, S1 soft, S3 at the apex. JVD visible with the head of the bed at 45 degrees. Pitting edema 2+ to mid-shin both legs. Abdomen soft, non-tender, no liver or spleen enlargement. Neuro intact.

Chest x-ray: perihilar opacities in a butterfly pattern with septal lines. ECG: sinus rhythm with LVH.
NT-proBNP 8,640 pg/mL. Creatinine 3.4 mg/dL, potassium 4.9 mmol/L.

Treatment: IV furosemide, supplemental oxygen, upright positioning.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology with acute decompensated heart failure.

NKDA.

reports.text: Left ventricle dilated with akinesis of the inferior wall and global hypokinesis of the remaining segments. Estimated ejection fraction 30%. reports.conclusion: Dilated left ventricle with EF 30% and inferior akinesis.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 12/20/2024 from the ED, discharged 12/24/2024.

Diagnosis: new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, acute decompensation; ischemic cardiomyopathy after prior inferior MI.

Course: diuresed with IV furosemide, about 4 kg net, with orthopnea and edema resolved by day 3 and room air saturations normal. Echo: dilated LV, EF 30%, inferior akinesis (EF 45% in 2022). Creatinine stayed near 3.4 through diuresis; potassium 4.9 on admission and stable. Moved to oral furosemide on day 3. Metoprolol succinate increased.

Discharge weight 93 kg - weigh every morning; call for a gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week.

Discharge medications:
- furosemide 40 mg every morning - NEW
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily - INCREASED from 25 mg
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime
- sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals
- calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily
- darbepoetin per nephrology
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed
- acetaminophen as needed
NKDA. Low-salt diet, 2 g sodium.

Follow-up: PCP within 7 days with BMP; heart failure clinic 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, discharged 12/24 with new heart failure. Pt and daughter on speaker. Breathing much better, sleeping in bed again with two pillows. Weighing each morning: 93.1 and 92.9 kg. Furosemide every morning, urinating a lot in the first few hours. New metoprolol dose picked up. Daughter is cooking low-salt. Visit 12/30 confirmed; BMP that day. ED record received and routed.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with daughter after admission 12/20-12/24 for new HFrEF, EF 30% (down from 45% after the 2022 MI), pulmonary edema, diuresed 4 kg. Discharge summary and ED note reviewed.

Since home: sleeping flat on two pillows, no night-time gasping. Ankles down. Walks the length of the house fine, slower on the porch steps. Daily weights steady around 93. No chest pain.

Meds reconciled with the discharge list: furosemide 40 qAM new; metoprolol succinate now 50; rest unchanged.

Exam: per flowsheet. JVP not elevated at 45 degrees. Lungs clear at the bases. Heart regular, no gallop today. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
1. HFrEF, ischemic, compensated now - furosemide 40, metoprolol 50, lisinopril 10. BMP today on the diuretic. Heart failure clinic mid-January. Daily weights, 2 g sodium, call parameters reviewed.
2. CKD 4 - BMP, results to nephrology.
3. CAD - aspirin, statin.
4. DM2 - glargine 24; watch for lows with less appetite.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of left kidney, except renal pelvis

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, with IV hydration before and after per renal protocol. Left kidney: heterogeneously enhancing solid mass arising from the lower pole, 7.0 cm in greatest dimension. Renal vein and IVC patent without tumor thrombus. Right kidney small, no mass, no hydronephrosis. No retroperitoneal or pelvic lymphadenopathy. Liver, adrenal glands, pancreas and spleen unremarkable. No osseous lesions. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: 7 cm enhancing left renal mass consistent with renal cell carcinoma. No evidence of metastatic disease.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for sending Mr. Dabrowski, 73, seen 12/23/2025 for weight loss he did not intend, intermittent flank pain on the left and blood in the urine. Background of CKD stage 4 from diabetic nephropathy, ischemic HFrEF with EF 30%, two coronary stents, and a 40 pack-year smoking history, quit 2022.

Exam: a firm mass is palpable in the left flank; it is not tender. No lymph nodes enlarged.

Labs: hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, WBC 7,500/uL, platelets 250,000/uL, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL, calcium 10.8 mg/dL. Urinalysis with red cells.

CT abdomen with contrast the same day (hydration protocol given his kidney function): 7 cm left renal mass, no evidence of spread.

Assessment: left renal cell carcinoma, clinically localized.

Plan: with stage 4 CKD, removing the whole kidney would likely leave him on dialysis, so I recommend a robotic left partial nephrectomy to save as much kidney as possible. Surgical risk is higher with his heart function, and I have asked cardiology for a pre-operative assessment. Nephrology aware. Aspirin may continue.

NKDA.

Urology

documents.title: Kidney surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The urologist wants to take part of my left kidney out. My daughter and I want to know if you think that's the right thing with my heart. Can we talk before I see the heart doctor next week?

documents.title: RE: Kidney surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Stan. I read the urologist's letter. A tumor that size should come out, and taking only part of the kidney is the right way to protect what kidney function you have. Your heart makes surgery riskier, which is exactly why they asked cardiology to weigh in first. I've booked you a visit with me on 1/20, after the cardiology appointment, so you, your daughter and I can go over everything together.

documents.title: Pre-operative cardiology assessment
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleagues,

Seen 1/13/2026 before planned robotic left partial nephrectomy. Ischemic cardiomyopathy, EF 30%, compensated, NYHA II. No angina. Stents in LAD (2022) and RCA (2022). Euvolemic on exam.

Assessment: elevated but acceptable perioperative cardiac risk for a necessary cancer operation. No further testing would change management.

Recommendations: continue aspirin through surgery; continue metoprolol succinate including the morning of surgery; hold furosemide and lisinopril the morning of surgery and resume when eating and pressure allows; careful fluid balance; telemetry post-op.

Cardiology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Pre-op visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with daughter to talk through the planned partial nephrectomy (2/10). Urology and cardiology letters reviewed together. He understands the cancer is confined to the kidney on CT, that the operation aims to cure it, and that his heart and kidneys raise the risk. He wants to proceed. Daughter will stay with him after.

No chest pain, weights stable, sleeping flat.

Exam: per flowsheet. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

Plan: BMP and A1c for the surgical team. Furosemide and lisinopril held morning of surgery as cardiology advised.

reports.text: Specimen: left kidney, lower pole, partial nephrectomy. Gross: well-circumscribed golden-yellow tumor, 7.0 cm in greatest dimension, with a rim of normal parenchyma. Microscopic: clear cell renal cell carcinoma, ISUP grade 2. No sarcomatoid or rhabdoid features. Tumor confined to the kidney; no perinephric fat or renal sinus invasion. Surgical margins negative.
reports.conclusion: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma, 7.0 cm, ISUP grade 2, margins negative, pT1b.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Admitted 2/10/2026 for robotic left partial nephrectomy; discharged 2/13/2026.

Operation: robot-assisted left lower pole partial nephrectomy. Uncomplicated. Minimal blood loss, no transfusion.

Pathology: clear cell renal cell carcinoma, 7.0 cm, ISUP grade 2, margins negative, pT1b.

Course: telemetry without events. Creatinine peaked at 3.9 on day 1 and was 3.5 at discharge. Fluids managed with cardiology input; furosemide and lisinopril resumed day 2. Walking the halls by day 1. Drain removed day 2.

Discharge medications: unchanged home list - aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, furosemide 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg, darbepoetin per nephrology, nitroglycerin as needed, acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed for incision pain.
NKDA.

Follow-up: urology clinic in 4 weeks; PCP for kidney labs in about 4 to 8 weeks; surveillance imaging in about 6 months.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge 2/13. Sore at the port sites, acetaminophen enough. Urine clear, no blood. Eating small meals, sugars 120s-180s, no lows. Weights 84-85. Breathing fine. Daughter staying through the week. Urology visit 3/10 booked. PCP visit set for mid-April with labs.

documents.title: Urology post-operative visit
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Seen 3/10/2026, four weeks after robotic left partial nephrectomy. Incisions healed. No hematuria since surgery. Flank pain gone. Pathology reviewed with him: clear cell RCC, 7.0 cm, grade 2, negative margins, pT1b, no adjuvant treatment indicated.

Surveillance: CT chest and renal ultrasound in July (non-contrast given his kidneys), then every 6 months for the first years.

Urology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after robotic L partial nephrectomy for clear cell RCC, 7.0 cm, grade 2, margins negative, pT1b. Urology visit in March: healed, surveillance imaging in July. No blood in the urine since surgery. Flank ache gone. Appetite better; weight steady at 84, no further loss since February.

Heart: no orthopnea, no edema, weights flat. No chest pain.

Exam: per flowsheet. Port sites healed. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Feet intact.

Labs today: creatinine 3.5 (was 3.1 before surgery), calcium 9.6.

A/P
1. L renal cell carcinoma s/p partial nephrectomy - urology surveillance July. Hematuria resolved; weight loss has stopped, off the active list.
2. CKD 4 - creatinine a notch higher after losing kidney tissue, as expected. Copy to nephrology.
3. HFrEF, CAD - stable on current regimen.
4. DM2 - A1c today, glargine 24.
5. Plan to see him in the summer; front desk to call him with a date once his July imaging is set.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stan, A1c 7.4 - the best it's been in years. Kidney number 3.5, a little higher than before surgery as we expected, and calcium is normal. Blood count is fine. I've sent these to your kidney doctor.
